channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
item.description:
Jordan Watkins SF Wide Receiver

Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

item.title: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, who managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 73 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evens is expected to miss the team’s Week 8 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into addition volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 53 yards on nine receptions.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey set a season high with 25 touches and 26 opportunities in a game played without Deebo Samuel and in which Mike Evans departed just before the half with an aggravation of his Achilles injury. The veteran workhorse back again proved how high his ceiling can be with such a robust role through the air. A second quarter fumble was his first lost fumble since 2024, a stretch spanning over 500 touches since he last lost a fumble. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 despite a difficult matchup on the ground against the Falcons in Week 7.

item.title: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break. The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

While the end line looks good in the box score, the fact that Diggs continued to operate in a situational role following the departure of Terry McLaurin in the first quarter was somewhat concerning for the veteran receiver’s upside potential in McLaurin’s absence, although the fact that he came into the game listed as questionable with a hamstring injury could have influenced his snap rate. Either way, Diggs continues to produce when on the field, returning significant value for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick for his services this summer. Diggs will be an upside WR3 when the Commanders take on the division rival Eagles in Week 8 following their bye.

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-4 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

While the yardage total looks solid on paper, the fact that Williams had only four targets in a game in which veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin departed in the first quarter and quarterback Jayden Daniels attempted 40 passes in concerning. Williams continues to flash big play upside through a multitude of injuries to teammates but has yet to fully take advantage of the increase in opportunity, something fantasy managers will hope corrects when the Commanders come out of their bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 4-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks stepped into an increased role in the offense following the first quarter injury to Terry McLaurin, the latter of whom appears to have suffered a significant knee injury. The six targets ranked third on the team behind tight end Chig Okonkwo and veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, but a late injury could immediately halt his momentum. Burks was injured on a contested ball in the end zone on fourth down with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and was escorted to the locker room by training staff. Fantasy managers interested in a potential waiver addition will want to track updates from the team regarding his health in the coming days.

item.title: 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports Mike Evans’ Achilles is intact but he is expected to “miss a little time.”
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Chan speculates that the window for his recovery could align with the team’s Week 8 bye week, meaning Evans would miss just one game with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable heading into Monday Night Football against the Commanders. All things considered, it’s solid news for Evans, the 49ers, and his fantasy managers. Expect a more concrete update from the team in the coming days as they limp into a Week 7 game against the Falcons down plentiful impact wide receivers.

Source: Jennifer Lee Chan

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

item.title: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

item.title: Jayden Daniels completed 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ 23-17, Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 10 yards on four carries.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

The Commanders gained just 90 yards of total offense and ran just 17 offensive plays in the first half, taking a 20-3 deficit into the break. Two quick touchdown drives to end the third quarter and begin the fourth quarter had the team in position to pull off an improbable comeback but two critical errors from Daniels sank that effort. The first error occurred on fourth down in the red zone with just over two minutes to play, when the team was late to break the huddle and ended up taking their first timeout down by six. They would fail to convert but would get the ball back with no timeouts and 52 seconds left. Daniels then committed an intentional grounding penalty from the San Francisco 28 with 16 seconds left, which incurred a loss of down and a 10-second runoff on the clock. The game would end on the following play. That now makes consecutive contests with late-game clock mismanagement that cost the Commanders potential wins. Rumors continue to swirl about a potential coaching change as the Commanders limp into their bye at a 1-4-1 record.

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) limped to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 6 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans came into the game with two injury designations, ribs and Achilles, ultimately suiting up. He limped to the locker room with the help of training staff and was seen in the tunnel pointing to his Achilles. The 33-year-old receiver has been on the injury report for much of the season, with the most recent ailment potentially proving to be too much to play through. Expect an update from the team after the half. Evans caught 3-of-5 targets for 94 yards prior to departing. 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reported after the game that Evans’ Achilles is intact but will “miss a little time.”

Source: Jennifer Lee Chan

item.title: Terry McLaurin (knee) was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of Week 6 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

The mechanism of the injury did not look promising, with the veteran receiver buckling to the turf in non-contact fashion. It’s a devastating development for the 31-year-old receiver in what was the first game since Week 1 where Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and Stefon Diggs were healthy together. Expect further updates from the team as the game progresses, but it certainly appears as if McLaurin’s season could be in jeopardy. McLaurin caught his only target for 27 yards prior to departing. Rookie Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks are the most likely fill-ins for the remainder of the game, and, potentially, the season.

item.title: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo reports Steelers are expected to sign Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
item.description:
Marquez Valdes-Scantling PIT Wide Receiver

Say it ain’t so, a former Rodgers favorite set to rejoin him during his twilight tour. Valdes-Scantling is reportedly set to sign to the Pittsburgh practice squad and could work his way to the active roster considering the absence of Michael Pittman, the latter of whom was moved to injured reserve Saturday. There likely won’t be any fantasy value to speak of.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a “good chance” to play in Week 7.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Finally, some good news for both Seahawks fans and fantasy managers, alike, after the Seattle run game has gotten off to a sluggish start to the 2026 season. Charbonnet has been on the physically unable to perform list through the first six weeks of the season but appears likely to make his return to the active roster for a marquee matchup against the Chiefs in a game some would consider a must-win for the suddenly reeling Seahawks. Macdonald added that the veteran back would get a full week of practice this week before any decision was made. Fantasy managers can add Charbonnet from waivers, if available.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is active for Week 6 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans will gut it out in Week 6 as fellow wide receiver Deebo Samuel is unable to go. Look for the bulk of the aerial offense to flow through Evans, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey, the three of whom handily led the team in route participation a week ago following Samuel’s departure. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa, WR Deebo Samuel, S Marques Sigle, LB Garret Wallow, OT Enrique Cruz Jr., and DT Naquan Jones.

item.title: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs returns from a one-game absence due a hamstring injury. Although possible he sees his route participation curtailed, fantasy managers that made it this far are likely forced to ride with the veteran receiver in a solid schematic matchup against the zone-heavy 49ers. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Marcus Mariota, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, OLB T.J. Magunranyanga, G Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu.

item.title: Seahawks activated Anthony Bradford’s 21-day practice window.
item.description:
Anthony Bradford SEA Guard

Bradford was placed on injured reserve after Week 1, seeing his first step to a return processed with the activation of his 21-day practice window. Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Monday that the veteran guard has a “really good chance” to return for Sunday Night Football against the Chiefs in Week 7.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Packers signed DT Mazi Smith, formerly of the Dolphins.
item.description:
Mazi Smith GB Defensive Tackle

Smith, a former first-round pick by the Cowboys in 2023, appeared in one game for the Dolphins earlier this season and has appeared in just nine games since 2025. The 25-year-old lineman has tallied 57 tackles and two sacks in his career and wouldn’t be asked to serve as anything more than added depth for the Packers if he were elevated to the 53-man roster.

item.title: Rams placed DL Kobie Turner (groin) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Kobie Turner

It’s a tough injury for Turner, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and will miss at least four weeks. He’s been a mainstay of Los Angeles’ defense over his first three years with several high-hurry seasons and stellar run defense. The Rams interior defense has taken a big hit today.

item.title: Rams placed DT Poona Ford (biceps) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Poona Ford

It will end his season. Ford has been a find for the Rams the last two years as a premium run-stuffer. This injury will test their defensive line depth. The soon-to-be 31-year-old will be a release candidate after the season with an $11.08 million cap hit of which the Rams can save $9.25 million by cutting him.

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
item.description:
Davante Adams

Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Vikings designed Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) to return.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

His 21-day practice window will open; most of the reporting is that the Vikings expect him to play in Week 7. Assuming that’s the case, we expect to see him hit the ground running on the Wednesday practice report with at least a limited session and perhaps a full.

item.title: Commanders activated Jeremy McNichols (quad) off injured reserve.
item.description:
Jeremy McNichols WAS Running Back

He’ll likely be Washington’s third-string back tonight, but one thing that two years and five weeks of Dan Quinn being in charge have taught us is that no one ever expects that Jeremy McNichols takeover until it’s too late. The backfield mix in Washington is weak and anyone could emerge in a post-'Bill’ world.

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he is undecided on whether or not Josh Jacobs will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

LaFleur said Jacobs will log a full week of practice but also pointed out that the 28-year-old back has “missed the exposure to football” over the last several months while on the commissioner’s exempt list. Jacobs was reinstated by the league late last week and is eligible to play immediately, but whether or not he will be active next week is to be determined. We’ll see how this week unfolds, but it would be a bit surprising if Jacobs was inactive in a pivotal NFC North matcup.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Commanders activated CB Trey Amos (fibula) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Trey Amos WAS Cornerback

He’ll immediately step in as a starting corner after a long rehab from a broken fibula suffered last November. The Commanders are desperate for better outside cornerback play and will be hoping their 2025 second-rounder can provide it in a hurry.

item.title: Commanders placed Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to get the majority of the work from Weeks 6-9. The Commanders also brought Jeremy McNichols off injured reserve and signed him to the active roster.

item.title: Patriots placed Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Romeo Doubs NE Wide Receiver

Doubs was ruled out in the third quarter of Week 6’s win over the Jets and will now miss at least the next four games. With the Patriots’ bye not coming until Week 11, the earliest Doubs will be able to return to the field will be in Week 12 against the Chargers. Doubs has caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season and has been targeted more than four times in just one game. Doubs can be dropped in leagues that don’t allow players to be stashed on IR.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 6 game against the Commanders.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

He won’t be activated off injured reserve for this one, but he did practice three times this week and he may be a consideration for Week 7’s game if things continue to trend in this direction. This means Brandin Cooks should operate as San Francisco’s No. 2 wideout assuming Mike Evans plays.

item.title: Giants coach John Harbaugh, asked about the running back room, said carries are “earned” and told his players to “do something” in their opportunities and more will come.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

Tyrone Tracy appeared to do the most with his opportunities last week, scoring the game’s only two touchdowns. Najee Harris was bottled up and Cam Skattebo was soft benched while Devin Singletary led the team in snaps while they were in comeback mode for most of the second half. By the letter of what he’s offering here, Tracy is probably the player who should get the majority of the snaps against the Texans. In actuality, we have no idea what will happen here and this quote doesn’t really help us. “I don’t like (rotating backs) either,” Harbaugh said per The Athletic’s Dan Duggan after the game. “One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys have done that yet.” We suspect we’ll be diving beat writer opinions ahead of Sunday.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said OC Sean Mannion will continue to call plays.
item.description:
Sean Mannion PHI Offensive Coordinator

Mannion is in his first year as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator and has struggled to turn around an offense that ranked 19th in scoring and 24th in total yards last season. The loss of Jalen Hurts (blood clots) will only further complicate life for Mannion and the Eagles, who rank 28th in points scored through six games this season. While Sirianni did say “everything’s on the table” to fix the offense, it doesn’t sound like any dramatic changes are coming just yet.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Bills signed CB Tre’Davious White to their practice squad.
item.description:
Tre'Davious White BUF Cornerback

The 31-year-old will be the latest veteran-as-practice-squadder bit corner in Buffalo’s beleaguered room. He has a storied history with the organization and is clearly still a very smart player.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Giants coach John Harbaugh said they’re “working through that now” when asked which quarterback would start against the Texans in Week 7.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

The fact that he has to think about it probably tips the hand that it will be J.J. McCarthy sooner or later — if not outright now. Jameis Winston was replaced by McCarthy in the fourth quarter yesterday and McCarthy showcased his deep arm and almost erased a large deficit by throwing for 243 yards on 21 attempts. If McCarthy did start against the Texans, he would likely be a bottom five superflex option on the Week 7 slate because of his established history as a starter.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Rams placed K Blake Grupe (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Blake Grupe

It’s a torn ACL for Grupe, who will now miss the rest of the season. The Rams will reshuffle the kicker deck again in Week 7, keep refreshing the page over the next few days to learn who it will be.

item.title: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee) will play in Week 7 against the Giants.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

Dell will make his long-awaited return next week against the Giants. By the time he takes the field in Week 7, Dell will have been more than 22 months removed from his last regular-season game, which came in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell suffered a torn ACL, LCL, and MCL, along with a dislocated knee, in that game against the Chiefs and has been on a long road to recovery. He’ll join a crowded receiver room that recently acquired Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel has posted a solid 17-334-2 line through the first six weeks of the season and topped 100 yards in Sunday’s win over the Jaguars. Targets could be hard to come by for Dell, but his return next week is an impressive feat on its own given the injury he had to work through.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, Adam Schefter said “the 49ers are optimistic” Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) will play in Week 6 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans did not log a practice in the days leading up to Monday night’s game against the Commanders, but the team still listed him as questionable on Saturday. Schefter reports the Niners want to see how Evans looks during pregame warmups, but it sounds like they are somewhat hopeful he will be active for Monday’s game. Evans has caught 24 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns this season and went for 7-113-1 on 10 targets in last week’s win over the Seahawks. He would be a must-start on Monday against Washington if he is active.

Source: Pat McAfee

item.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said there’s optimism that Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will “be fine.”
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Sounds like another week of managed reps in practice is ahead for Bateman, but he’ll likely have a reasonable chance to suit up in Week 7.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamark Jackson (ankle) could “potentially” practice this week.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

When asked if Jackson’s ankle has improved over the last two weeks, Minter offered up a resounding “yes.” Jackson missed a second straight game in Week 6’s loss to the Browns, despite reports earlier in the week that said he nearly played in Week 5 against the Falcons. We’ve seen injuries linger in the past for Jackson, whose team fell to 4-2 on the season and is now preparing to face another division rival in the Bengals next week. Jackson, who is considered day-to-day, did not get on the practice field in any capacity last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an upgrade as far as his Week 7 availability is concerned.

Source: Ryan Mink

item.title: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
item.description:
C.J. Gardner-Johnson BUF Safety

Gardner-Johnson was caught on tape spitting at/in the direction of Raiders TE Brock Bowers after the two were seen jawing at one another after a play. Gardner-Johnson will be suspended without pay when the Bills return from their bye to play the Ravens in Week 8. He has tallied 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception this season while earning a PFF grade of 55.2.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said “Guys have to step up and make plays” when asked about benching Brian Thomas Jr. for the second half of Week 6’s loss to the Texans.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Coen benched Thomas for the entire second half after he had one drop and two non-catches in the first against Houston. It sure seems like the runway for Thomas is running out in Jacksonville. A potential trade is the only fantasy salvation coming for the third-year receiver as he looks buried here.

Source: ProFootballTalk on NBCSports.com

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Tom Pelissero’s report over the weekend was that Pierce was still weeks from returning, and unfortunately this very much aligns with that. Pierce is now eligible to return off injured reserve, but until we see him designated to return and practicing, it’s hard to believe he’s close to returning.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will remain the team’s starting quarterback against the Vikings in Week 7.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Jones has yet to crack 270 yards or throw multiple touchdowns in a start. He’s also thrown six interceptions and is completing a career-worst 59.6 percent of his passes. It is not an uncommon observation to say that he is struggling to drive the ball on his throws. While the Colts are not going away from Jones now, that does not necessarily mean he will remain the starter all year if he continues to play like this. Given what the Vikings have been up to this year, we’d be surprised if Jones escaped the bottom five of quarterback fantasy points this week.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he has not considered removing Bo Nix from the starting job.
item.description:
Bo Nix DEN Quarterback

“He is going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved. The improved play from our offensive line; the more efficient we are relative to downs; running the football. That’s our job as coaches here,” Payton said. Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league through six starts and Jay Glazer passed along word yesterday that Payton changed the terminology that OC Davis Webb had put in this offseason back to what it was last season, which apparently did not help Nix out. He’ll be hard to trust even with a slapdash Cardinals defense on tap for Week 7.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) is expected to miss time and it “could be an extended absence.”
item.description:
Elijah Arroyo SEA Tight End

Arroyo’s career hasn’t really got off the ground with AJ Barner as the obvious No. 1 in the Seahawks tight end room. The 50th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft has just two targets this year and hasn’t been a fantasy factor yet.

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) is “supposed to practice Wednesday.”
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Bowles has already said that the team is preparing as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7, but the team will be evaluating Mayfield to see how he is progressing in his recovery from a dislocated thumb. Mayfield reportedly pushed to play last week after throwing on Monday, but his thumb swelled up, which factored into the decision to sit him in Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. Given Bowles’ comments about the team’s plans entering the week, it sounds like Mayfield is at risk of missing at least one more game, but we’ll see how his hand responds when he gets on the field on Wednesday.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sauce Gardner is considered week-to-week after suffering a calf strain in Week 6’s loss to the Titans.
item.description:
Sauce Gardner IND Cornerback

According to Rapoport, an MRI revealed a mild calf strain for Gardner, who is expected to be week-to-week with the injury. While he is expected to miss some time, Rapoport also notes that Gardner is not expected to miss “an extended period,” which suggests he won’t be placed on injured reserve. Gardner sounds like a virtual lock to miss Week 7’s game against the Vikings, so we’ll see if a week away gives him enough time to be ready for Week 8’s game against the Jaguars. Gardner has totaled 17 tackles and four pass breakups for the Colts this season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 62.6.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said the team is planning as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Jalon Daniels TB Quarterback

Bowles said this week will be an important evaluation week for Baker Mayfield, who is still rehabbing a dislocated thumb that has sidelined him since Week 3. Daniels hasn’t been overly impressive in his three starts this season, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions while also taking nine sacks. That said, he did manage to pull off a win over the Cowboys in Week 5 and had the Buccaneers in position to beat the Steelers in Week 6 before Pittsburgh erupted for 16 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime. We’ll see how things unfold throughout the week, but it sounds like Mayfield is at least one week away from returning. Daniels would be on the fantasy radar as a low-end QB2 if he gets the start against Carolina.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Dan Patrick of The Dan Patrick Show said a source familiar with the Colts’ GM situation told him the team’s “first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning.”
item.description:
Peyton Manning

Patrick isn’t a reporter we go to often here, but he’s a well-connected veteran in the industry. According to Patrick, his source said the call with Manning will not only be to get the names of potential candidates for the GM vacancy but also to “explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in being a general manager for the Colts as the entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts.” Mannings’ connection to the Colts doesn’t need to be explained to anyone, but it’s far too early to say whether Manning has any interest in the role. Long-time GM Chris Ballard was recently relieved of his duties, and the Colts will likely speak to several candidates to fill the role in the offseason. Manning has not been involved in any football front office roles since retiring after the 2015 season.

Source: Dan Patrick Show

item.title: Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds will lead the team’s personnel department for the remainder of the season.
item.description:
Ed Dodds IND Front Office

With the Colts sitting on a 2-4 record and the trade deadline 22 days away, Dodds could be involved in some key roster decisions over the next three weeks. Dodds was hired as the Colts’ vice president of player personnel in 2017 and has been a candidate for several GM openings over the last few offseasons. Depending on how things go the rest of the way, it’s possible Dodds earns a chance to be promoted to the Colts GM position next offseason after the team fired Chris Ballard earlier in the day.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 4-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

Lane was immediately involved in the offense after missing the previous four weeks with a wrist injury. The rookie third-rounder caught two of his four passes on the Ravens’ opening drive that ended with a short touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and ran 22 routes on the day. Zay Flowers (34) and Devontez Walker (26) both ran more routes than Lane on the afternoon, but Lane has been targeted on 21.1 percent of his routes in limited action this season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to start him in Week 7 against the Bengals, but the early volume is encouraging for a player who was hyped up throughout training camp.

item.title: Jordan Davis (ankle) told reporters x-rays were negative on his ankle and he feels “OK” at this point.
item.description:
Jordan Davis PHI Defensive Tackle

Davis is still a candidate to be limited in practice this week, but it doesn’t look like this injury is a major threat to send him to injured reserve or anything like that. Talking with the media after the game is a good sign for his future ability.

Source: John Clark

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Hurts “will be out an estimated three months as he undergoes treatment” for blood clots.
item.description:
Jalen Hurts PHI Quarterback

This would effectively end Hurts’ season, as a three-month absence would have him on track to return some time in late-January/early-February. In a statement released by Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lyyn, she said further tests revealed “deep vein thrombosis as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli.” She said that Hurts is stable and is not expected to have any “functional limitations” and that his treatment to resolve his blood clotting issues “should only involve anticoagulation [i.e., ‘blood thinners’].” As a result, Hurts will not be permitted to engage in football activities and will not be allowed to resume them until he is off his blood thinners. The good news here is that Hurts is expected to make a full recovery, and the doctors do not believe this will have a long-term effect on him moving forward. Hurts threw for 933 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions this season while completing 57.8 percent of his passes — his lowest mark since his rookie season. He ran for another 107 yards and one touchdown as he and the Eagles struggled in his first five starts under offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. He remains under contract through the 2028 season, but Hurts has faced his fair share of scrutiny since leading the Eagles to a Super Bowl title in 2024. Hurts’ contract situation would suggest his job is more than secured for the foreseeable future, but this is the same Eagles front office that used a 2020 second round pick to select him as the heir apparent to Carson Wentz, who signed a four-year extension with the team in 2019. While we fully expect Hurts to be back with the Eagles next season, we can’t rule out the team using an early draft pick on a quarterback in a draft that is projected to be one of the more QB-rich drafts in recent memory. Tanner McKee, who started Week 6’s game against the Panthers, will take over as the team’s starter going forward.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Falcons released Cooper Rush.
item.description:
Cooper Rush

Rush’s release came after the Falcons signed Andy Dalton. Rush had a rough stretch with the Falcons, throwing for 229-1-4 in his two starts while completing 56.4 percent of his passes. Once regarded as one of the better backup quarterbacks in the league, Rush has struggled mightily in his two seasons away from the Cowboys, going 0-4 in his starts since 2024 while throwing one touchdown to eight interceptions. He could catch on elsewhere as a practice squad option in the coming days, but he seems like a long shot to start another game in 2026.

item.title: Bam Knight suffered from “full body cramps” for much of the second half of Arizona’s Week 6 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

The good news is that this shouldn’t exactly be expected to sideline Knight going forward after his 98-total yard effort against the Rams. Knight’s fantasy value is tenuous despite the big game, as he was outsnapped by Tyler Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love (ankle) could be back next week. But he did outplay Allgeier in Week 6.

Source: Cardinals.com

item.title: Falcons signed Andy Dalton, formerly of the Eagles.
item.description:
Andy Dalton ATL Quarterback

Dalton had a chance to re-sign with the Eagles after being let go by them earlier in the week, but he spurned them to sign with Atlanta. The 38-year-old vet will presumably serve as the Falcons’ third-string QB for now, but could be one injury away from seeing playing time. Dalton threw for 293-1-1 on 37 pass attempts for the Panthers last season and has not started more than five games in a season since 2022.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Colts fired GM Chris Ballard.
item.description:
Chris Ballard

The team announced its decision to move on from Ballard early Monday morning. The Colts opted to retain Ballard for a 10th season earlier this offseason despite a monumental collapse in the second half of last season that saw the team finish 8-9 after getting off to an 8-2 start. Ballard was hired as the Colts GM in 2017 and leaves with just two postseason berths and zero division titles to his name. The abrupt retirement of Andrew Luck before the start of the 2018 season presented an early challenge for Ballard to suddenly find a new QB, which often resulted in short-term answers to solve a long-term problem. After the likes of Philip Rivers, Matt Ryan, and Carson Wentz passed through the organization, the Colts finally selected Anthony Richardson in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft in hopes of landing their guy. When it became apparent Richardson wasn’t the answer, the team signed Daniel Jones, who turned in a solid 2025 campaign and was rewarded with a two-year, $88 million contract earlier this offseason. Among the multiple missteps by Ballard during his Colts tenure is the trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner, whom he acquired in exchange for the team’s 2026 and 2027 first-round picks. Few GMs get the leash that Ballard was provided with by the Colts, but this felt like a move that was destined to happen now or at the end of the season. Now, the Colts can get a head start on their next GM search in what is shaping up to be another rough season. The team announced that head coach Shane Steichen will remain in his role for now.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said he “can’t answer that now” when asked about who his starting quarterback would be heading into Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

It’s the exact kind of answer we would expect from a coach who is just minutes removed from his team nearly completing a comeback victory. J.J. McCarthy stepped in for Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter and lit up the Saints for 243 yards and one touchdown in the fourth quarter, leading the Giants on three scoring drives and 17 unanswered points in a game that the Saints won 34-27. Whether it’s in Week 7 or a point later in the season, McCarthy feels like a lock to start multiple games for the Giants, who now sit at 3-2-1 on the season. The Jameis Winston Experience, while fun, is often short-lived, and his underwhelming performance on Sunday against the Saints (152-1-2) comes a week after Winston struggled for the entire first half against the Commanders before he turned it on in the second half. Harbaugh will likely announce his Week 7 starter in the coming days, but it wouldn’t be surprising to learn the team is handing McCarthy the keys for the remainder of the season.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) traveled with the team to Paris for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

The Saints have not opened Tyson’s 21-day window for return, but the fact that he traveled with the team suggests his window could be opened later this week, which would allow him to begin practicing with the team. There’s some belief that Tyson could return in Week 9 after the Saints’ bye week, but the team hasn’t committed to a return date for him just yet. We wouldn’t expect Tyson to suit up this week against the Steelers.

Source: New Orleans Football Network

item.title: Savion Williams caught all four targets for 32 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding nine yards on two carries.
item.description:
Savion Williams GB Wide Receiver

Williams was immediately asked to fill the WR3 role for an offense missing its top two slot receivers. Even so, he finished fifth on the team in targets and carries little fantasy value with Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft ahead of him. That doesn’t change ahead of a matchup with the Lions in Week 7.

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

item.title: Christian Watson caught 3-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson drew lockdown corner Joey Porter Jr. for much of the game, something that aided teammate Matthew Golden in leading the team in both targets and receiving in the win. The talented fifth-year receiver is already within 74 yards of setting a new career high in receiving while also being just one touchdown shy of a new high water mark, two achievements he will look to unlock when the Packers face off against the Lions in a potential shootout in Week 7. Watson remains a back-end WR1 for that matchup.

item.title: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden took advantage of being the Green Bay receiver to mostly avoid Joey Porter Jr., although he did victimize the lockdown corner on a 37-yard reception in the first quarter. He would cash in on a touchdown eight plays later from nine yards out for his third score of the season. The speedy second-year receiver has now eclipsed 100 yards in half of his games while hitting 95 in one other, and is pacing for over 1,400 yards and eight touchdowns. That’s enough to have Golden in the conversation for one of the top values of fantasy drafts this summer. Golden will be an upside WR2 when the Packers take on the division rival Lions in Week 7.

item.title: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
item.description:
Pierre Strong GB Running Back

Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

item.title: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

item.title: Jake Ferguson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson has now been out-targeted by the team’s WR3, Ryan Flournoy, in five of six games, even being out-targeted by fellow tight end Brevyn Span-Ford in this one. The latter caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards on a night quarterback Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Any fleeting fantasy value is quickly evaporating as the fourth option, at best, through the air. Ferguson can safely be left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Eagles on the road.

item.title: Ryan Flournoy caught 7-of-9 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Ryan Flournoy DAL Wide Receiver

While the yardage totals continue to remain modest for the third-year receiver, his emergence as a trusted WR3 in the offense has led to him out-targeting tight end Jake Ferguson in five of six games through the first third of the season. That’s a role that can return usable FLEX production in the right matchups in the typically high-powered Cowboys offense, adding to his high-end handcuff value. Fantasy managers can continue to stash FLournoy ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the division rival Eagles.

item.title: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
CeeDee Lamb DAL Wide Receiver

Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through an up-and-down connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

item.title: George Pickens caught 6-of-11 targets for 73 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens was targeted just once in the first half as the Cowboys were held under 100 yards of total offense before the break. He would remain quiet through the third quarter, adding a single catch to his ledger on two additional targets before seeing eight looks in the final frame with the Cowboys in desperation mode. The 11 targets finished second on the team to CeeDee Lamb’s 18 while the 73 yards slightly edged the 70 of Lamb. Pickens remains an upside WR2 ahead of a divisional matchup against the inside-funnel Eagles’ secondary in Week 7.

item.title: Javonte Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding nine yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Javonte Williams DAL Running Back

Williams has now been held to 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in five of six games and 45 yards on the ground or fewer in four of six games, with seven combined touchdowns keeping his fantasy value afloat through the first third of the regular season. Williams has now seen 12 or fewer carries in four of six contests to start the year. The good news is that the Cowboys have no choice but to keep riding Williams until the wheels fall off considering the general lack of depth in the backfield, meaning there are likely to be better days ahead for the veteran back. He gets another middling matchup on the ground against the division rival Eagles in Week 7, where he will be a volume-driven RB2.

item.title: Dak Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 23-13, Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding seven yards on two carries.
item.description:
Dak Prescott DAL Quarterback

Prescott and the Cowboys were completely unable to get anything going prior to the half, managing just 92 yards of total offense while taking a 17-point deficit into the break. They would force a three-and-out to start the third quarter and follow it up with a touchdown drive to get on the board, but a punt and two turnovers on downs left them trailing by 16 until a late score inside of two minutes remaining in the final frame. Prescott’s two interceptions occurred deep in Green Bay territory in the second quarter, removing much needed points from the scoreboard in what was then a tight game. The loss drops the Cowboys to 2-4 and looking up at the Giants for the division lead through a third of the regular season. Prescott will be a back-end QB1 on the road against the division rival Eagles in Week 7.

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Blake Grupe suffered a knee injury in their Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Blake Grupe

Bringing back Harrison Mevis, whom the Rams waived five days ago, is one option, but it is unclear whether either side wants a reunion. The Rams might want to bring a few special teams contributors aboard while they’re at it. Grupe was injured during a tackle attempt because yet another return had scooted right past the Rams’ special teams coverage unit. The Rams rank outside the top 25 in average kick return yards allowed and average punt return yards allowed. Minimizing kicker tackling attempts in the future is probably a good call.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
item.description:
Blake Corum

Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

item.title: Kyren Williams rushed 10 times for 50 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 17 yards.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

Williams played for the duration of the first and third drives, ceding the second to Blake Corum, who played well right out of the gate. The duo rotated during drives thereafter. Williams looked like his normal, capable self, showcasing a slick spin move off contact on the Rams’ fourth drive. Unfortunately for him, Corum fought hard to convert a first down just inside the red zone and coach Sean McVay kept him out there for the scoring-position sequence, which ended in a 15-yard receiving score for Corum. Williams quietly continued his high-end receiving involvement, earning six targets against the Cardinals today. Williams belongs in the RB1 tier next week against the Raiders.

item.title: Tyler Higbee caught 4-of-4 targets for 22 yards and one lost fumble in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Tyler Higbee

Higbee lost volume to Colby Parkinson in this one. Higbee also had the ball ripped from his possession by Cardinals LB Cody Simon while trying to fall forward for extra yards on the Rams’ seventh drive, further reducing his fantasy output. With Parkinson playing well, Higbee is a shakier, low-end TE1 against the Raiders next week.

item.title: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson played effectively against the Cardinals’ zone coverage this afternoon. He bagged a first down after finding a soft spot downfield on the Rams’ fourth drive, and deftly hurdled a defender on a one-yard gain a few plays later. His touchdown occurred on the Rams’ final possession and required post-catch effort, barreling through contact and extending for the score. Parkinson is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Raiders in Week 7.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews ran 11 more routes than rookie tight end Josh Cuevas but was out-targeted by Cuevas 5-to-3. Andrews continues to underwhelm in the passing game and has now failed to surpass 28 yards in four straight games. He can be left on waivers ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals.

item.title: Jaleel McLaughlin rushed nine times for 41 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 14 additional yards.
item.description:
Jaleel McLaughlin CLE Running Back

McLaughlin operated as the Browns’ lead back with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson both sidelined. The 26-year-old back saw six of his carries go for four or more yards, and he was the only Browns running back to see a target. If either Judkins or Sampson are able to return in Week 7 against the Titans, McLaughlin will likely return to his role as a lightly used backup. If Judkins were to miss another game, McLaughlin could be in line for double digit touches, but he would be a risky bet as far as fantasy is concerned.

item.title: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

This was the worst game of Boston’s young career. After going for 40-plus yards in his first five games to start the season, the promising rookie was blanketed in coverage all afternoon and managed just one reception as a result. Boston may have had a chance at scoring were it not for a pass near the right side of the end zone sailing too far out of bounds for him to bring both feet down, but scoring opportunities were hard to come by in this one. Boston will be back on the fantasy radar as a WR3 next week against the Titans.

item.title: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that there is “growing buzz” that the Chargers could fire OC Mike McDaniel “soon,” and potentially replace him with pass game specialist Adam Gase.
item.description:
Mike McDaniel LAC Offensive Coordinator

According to Florio, Gase “is expected to take over if McDaniel is fired.” The Chargers go on bye in Week 7, so this is the best time to install a new offense if they really intend to do so. Gase previously served as head coach of the Jets and Dolphins, though those stints are hardly reassuring. His offenses have frequently fallen short of expectations. The 0-6 Chargers are searching for answers, though, and the McDaniel-Justin Herbert pairing does not seem to be working out.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Davante Adams

Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack. Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

item.title: Noah Gray caught all three of his targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Noah Gray KC Tight End

The Chiefs used more two tight end sets with Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton sidelined. Gray ran a route on around half of KC’s drop backs and matched Travis Kelce with 53 yards. If Kelce struggles to play through the ankle injury he picked up against the Bolts, Gray could step in as the team’s TE1 in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

item.title: Cyrus Allen caught both of his targets for 27 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

Rashee Rice’s absence didn’t translate into more playing time for Allen, who logged a mere five pass routes against the Chargers. He can remain on waiver wires until his playing time increases, which is unlikely if Rice is able to return in the coming weeks.

item.title: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington’s nine carries were only one fewer than the 10 Ashton Jeanty saw on the night, but Washington was by far the more productive back. The rookie fourth-rounder averaged a solid 4.8 YPC in this one and ripped off an 18-yard run in the fourth quarter on a drive that ended with a Tre Tucker touchdown. Jeanty is dealing with a foot/ankle injury that is clearly limiting him on the field. Washington should continue to spell Jeanty in Week 7 against the Rams, but he doesn’t have much to offer fantasy managers as far as reliable production is concerned. He continues to be nothing more than a stash as long as Jeanty is active and on the field.

item.title: Puka Nacua caught 6-of-7 targets for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

The Cardinals’ pass rush derailed the Rams’ offensive game plan early on, and Nacua was held without a target until just under 11 minutes remaining in the second quarter. Heartbreak struck on the Rams’ sixth drive. Nacua shook his coverage defender on a hitch-and-go and had no one between him and the end zone. Matthew Stafford let it rip, but was hit during the throw. Nacua dove for what should have been a 65-yard touchdown, but the pass fell incomplete. Nacua had another close call late in the game, dragging a defender for half of his downfield route, on what was ultimately flagged for DPI, but the defender’s unscrupulous tactic prevented Nacua from hauling in a 45-yarder at the Cardinals’ 10-yard line. Fortunately, Nacua and Stafford linked up for 42- and 16-yard gains on their lone touchdown-scoring drive at the end of the game, salvaging Nacua’s box score. He’s an elite WR1 against the Raiders next week.

item.title: Emmett Johnson had three rushes for six yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

It was another Ken Walker explosion game (128 yards, two touchdowns on the ground) with Johnson serving as the breather back. Johnson should be rostered as a high-upside contingency option in case Walker misses any time in the coming weeks or months.

item.title: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Jalen Nailor LV Wide Receiver

After missing Week 5’s game against the Patriots due to a concussion, Nailor was back on the field this week to face the Bills. Unfortunately for the 2026 free-agent signee, the results looked all too familiar. Nailor managed only one reception for nine yards and is now sitting on a 6-61-0 receiving line through his first five games of the season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be counting on him to provide anything in next week’s game against the Rams.

item.title: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

item.title: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Matthew Stafford

The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Puka Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

item.title: Theo Wease caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Theo Wease LAC Wide Receiver

Wease ran a route on 28 of the team’s 45 drop backs while the Chargers struggled with a spate of wide receiver injuries. Wease could see some playing time when the Chargers come back from their Week 7 bye if Ladd McConkey (head) remains sidelined. Wease had one reception headed into Week 6.

item.title: Charlies Kolar caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Kolar ran 28 routes on the day while Oronde Gadsden II ran 24 routes and also had five targets from Justin Herbert. The division of pass-catching duties for LA’s tight ends make both players unplayable for fantasy outside the deepest formats.

item.title: Kimani Vidal had seven rushes for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 19 yards.
item.description:
Kimani Vidal LAC Running Back

Vidal got much of his work in the first quarter before Omarion Hampton worked into the backfield later in the game. Hampton ended up leading the Bolts backfield in both routes and targets, with Vidal a close second in both categories. When the Chargers return from the bye week, Vidal could see an increased role as the team looks elsewhere for production. He should be rostered in most deep formats.

item.title: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day. (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards.) Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either player to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

item.title: When asked if Chargers OC Mike McDaniel is going to continue calling plays, coach Jim Harbaugh said the team is “going to look at everything.”
item.description:
Mike McDaniel LAC Offensive Coordinator

Harbaugh made clear that his team has to “address everything,” especially the offense, and acknowledged that the Chargers aren’t scoring enough points. He added that the plan is to watch today’s game tape and “get with our offensive coaches” to figure things out. Although McDaniel could end up losing play-calling duties, Harbaugh owned the team’s offensive woes, saying it “starts” with him.

Source: Anthony Gharib

item.title: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell had two rushes for four yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell did not catch his only target on the day. He was third among Bolts running backs in pass routes, behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. The sad state of the Chargers offense and injuries to the team’s offensive line make it nearly impossible for Mitchell to post fantasy relevant numbers for now. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7.

item.title: Brock Bowers caught 4-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.i
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

After being held without so much as a target in the first half of Sunday’s loss, Bowers still managed to finish the day with 70 receiving yards on a team-high nine targets. The Bills effectively shadowed Bowers with cornerback Christian Benford for much of the game but Bowers took advantage of a few holes in the Bills’ zone defense to make a few plays, which included back-to-back catches of 18 and 29 yards in the fourth quarter. Bowers did in one half what most tight ends need a full game to do, which speaks to his ability as one of the top play-making tight ends in the league. He’ll remain on the TE1 radar next week against the Rams.

item.title: Chad Ryland converted 6-of-6 field goals in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Chad Ryland ARI Kicker

Ryland attempted and converted a season-high six field goals today, including two between the 20-29-yard lines, three between the 30-39-yard lines and one from 40-plus. He’s attempted fewer than three field goals in 3-of-6 games thus far, and coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he “never” wants to see Ryland attempt six kicks again, unless they are extra points. Ryland should probably not be counted on for high-end K1 results next week against the Broncos.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: KeAndre Lambert-Smith caught 5-of-10 targets for 32 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
item.description:
KeAndre Lambert-Smith LAC Wide Receiver

With Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Lambert-Smith led the Chargers in pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with the opportunity. The flurry of Chargers wideout injuries could leave the team with no choice but to give Lambert-Smith significant snaps when they return from their Week 7 bye.

item.title: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Packers.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

Turpin departed before the first offensive play run from scrimmage after sustaining a ribs injury on the opening kickoff. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays and is listed as questionable to return by the team.

item.title: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Tucker found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 23-23. Later in the game, with the Raiders down by 10, Tucker found himself on the receiving end of a Kirk Cousins moon ball in the end zone, which he hauled in for a 44-yard touchdown to cut the Bills’ lead to 33-30 with just over a minute left in the game. Tucker is the closest thing the Raiders have to a fantasy-viable wide receiver, and he has proven to be a volatile player throughout his four-year career. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a boom-or-bust WR4 in next week’s game against the Rams.

item.title: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

item.title: Ken Walker had 19 rushes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding two catches for 11 yards.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

The Chiefs once again leaned hard on the rushing attack, running the ball 24 times while attempting 30 passes on the day. Walker breezed through a lifeless LA defense from start to finish. On many of his carries Walker was not touched until he was five or six yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Walker, who accounted for 19 of the team’s 24 rushing attempts, is perhaps the most important player in fantasy football through Week 6. He’ll be an RB1 in Week 7 against his former mates in Seattle.

item.title: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
item.description:
Pierre Strong GB Running Back

Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry that was overshadowed by the looking return of lead back Josh Jacobs, the latter of whom is expected to be activated from the commissioner exempt list Monday. Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

item.title: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
CeeDee Lamb DAL Wide Receiver

Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through a failing connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams must sign a new kicker after Blake Grupe suffered a knee injury in their Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Blake Grupe

Bringing back Harrison Mevis, whom the Rams waived five days ago, is one option, but it is unclear whether either side wants a reunion. The Rams might want to bring a few special teams contributors aboard while they’re at it. Grupe was injured during a tackle attempt because yet another return had scooted right past the Rams’ special teams coverage unit. The Rams rank outside the top 25 in average kick return yards allowed (28.9) and average punt return yards allowed (13.5). Minimizing kicker tackling attempts in the future is probably a good call.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Tyler Higbee caught 4-of-4 targets for 22 yards and one lost fumble in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Tyler Higbee

Higbee was simply outplayed by fellow TE Colby Parkinson in this one. Higbee also had the ball ripped from his possession by LB Cody Simon while trying to fall forward for extra yards on the Rams’ seventh drive, further reducing his fantasy output. With Parkinson playing well, Higbee is a shakier, low-end TE1 against the Raiders next week.

item.title: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards). Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either guy to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier rushed 18 times for 38 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams, adding one reception for 10 yards.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

Allgeier got the start, but looked slow compared to his backfield mate, Bam Knight, today. It was an extremely disappointing showing and the Cardinals seemingly leaned on Knight more and more as the game progressed. Allgeier still totaled 19 touches, including 18 carries, but he was routinely stopped around the line of scrimmage and critically ceded red zone snaps to Knight. Knight may have injured his right hand or wrist late in the game, but he continued playing. With Jerermiyah Love (ankle) currently sidelined, Allgeier could end up being the lead back again next week against the Broncos. Keep an eye on the Cardinals’ injury report this week.

item.title: Travis Kelce caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce was in and out of the lineup in the first half while dealing with a lingering ankle issue. Though he clearly wasn’t 100 percent, Kelce was second on the team (behind Xavier Worthy) in targets and had a 24-yard catch and run reception in the second half. Kelce, who now has nine catches over his past three games, should see more looks from Patrick Mahomes for as long as Rashee Rice (hamstring) is sidelined. He’ll be a top-15 fantasy play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-30 attempts for 272 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding five rushes for 16 yards.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Mahomes had multiple touchdown tosses in every game this season headed into Week 6. Kansas City’s offense didn’t have to do much against a sleepy Chargers offense that could barely move the ball once again on Sunday. The Chiefs leaned on Ken Walker, who went for 128 yards and two touchdowns on the day. With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton out, Mahomes relied heavily on Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. Until Rice is back and fully healthy, Mahomes will be more of a top-15 option. He gets the Seahawks in Week 7.

item.title: Bam Knight rushed 15 times for 80 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

Knight seemingly earned more work as the game progressed by simply outplaying Allgeier, the team’s Week 6 starter. After a few unproductive Allgeier runs, the Cardinals got Knight involved as a receiver on the second drive, his first catch coming via a slant route and generating a first down. They gave him three carries on the third drive, culminating in a 31-yarder on a well-blocked run to the left. Allgeier subbed in for the red zone sequence on that drive, but the coaching staff gave Knight three red zone touches on the fifth drive, compared to just one for Allgeier. They gave Knight two more red zone touches on the seventh drive. Blocking failed him on the second one, and it may have resulted in a right hand or wrist injury. Knight trotted over to the medical staff after the play, and a trainer could be seen stabilizing Knight’s wrist while putting him through sideline testing. Knight did return to the game on the next drive, but this is worth keeping an eye on. If Jeremiyah Love (ankle) misses the Cardinals’ Week 7 game against the Broncos, and Knight’s apparent injury is a non-issue, Knight could end up getting the start next week. Stay tuned.

item.title: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Shakir didn’t have an overly productive day through the air in this one, but he did manage to find the end zone for his first touchdown of the season. Shakir scored on a nine-yard screen pass in the second quarter to put the Bills up 13-7. Shakir has now gone for double-digit PPR points in three straight games but will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR4/WR5 in Week 8 when the Bills return from their bye to face the Ravens.

item.title: Trey McBride caught 7-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
